_comment: *** THIS CONFIG HARD-RESET THE NODE ON 2026-08-31T09:44Z. DO NOT RUN IT AS WRITTEN. *** It is kept at the sizing that crashed, quarantined by run.sh's budget preflight, because the failure is the most useful thing in this file. WHAT RAN: 2,000-token system prompt + 6 contexts x 21,000 = 128,021 tokens per request against max-model-len 131,072, ldp_num_permutations 2, ldp_num_inflight_requests 1. Permutation 0 completed cleanly -- 128,021 input tokens, TTFT 51,969 ms, decode 27.7 tok/s. Permutation 1 was dispatched at ~09:37:30, never completed, and the box reset at ~09:44 -- about 6.5 minutes in-flight on a request whose sibling took 52 seconds. WHY THE PREFLIGHT WAS RIGHT AND THE OVERRIDE WAS WRONG. run.sh computed the naive ldp_num_permutations x prompt x 29,696 = 7.60 GB against a 4.5 GB budget and REFUSED. It was overridden with BUDGET_GB=8 on the argument that lexicographic permutations share a prefix -- (0,1,2,3,4,5) then (0,1,2,3,5,4) share the first 4 contexts -- so only ~8 contexts of NEW keys would be written, about 5.05 GB, inside the 6 GiB L1. That reasoning is wrong twice over: (1) DEDUP REDUCES UNIQUE KEYS, NOT DISK TRAFFIC. LMCache writes THROUGH to the L2 fs adapter rather than only on L1 eviction -- directly observed earlier, L2 growing while L1 sat at 18%. Measured across this run: /kv-l2/bf16 went from 9.0 GB / 302 files to 15 GB / 508 files, so ~6 GB hit NVMe in roughly 90 seconds. That IS the sustained writeback the budget exists to prevent, and no amount of prefix sharing avoids it. (2) THE LOAD SIDE WAS IGNORED ENTIRELY. Permutation 1's shared prefix is ~86,000 tokens, which it must FETCH from L1/L2 while simultaneously storing the moved suffix. Concurrent bulk load + store is what multiplies the simultaneously-pinned CUDA-IPC transfer buffers -- the acute half of the documented crash mechanism (BENCHMARK-HANDOFF.md section 3). A budget counting only stored bytes cannot see it. Note the perverse consequence: a HIGHER cache hit rate makes this workload MORE dangerous, not less. MEMORY WAS NOT THE SIGNAL, AGAIN. The last sample before the reset (09:38:03) showed 99.91 GiB available. /sys/fs/pstore has mtime 09:44 and is EMPTY -- the kernel emitted nothing, matching the netconsole silence recorded for crashes 1-4. bench.log stops at 09:38:12 at exactly 61,440 bytes, a page-cache boundary, so everything after was lost to the reset; there is no bench_results.csv or bench_summary.json for this run, unlike the three that completed. TO RUN A PERMUTATOR ON THIS VARIANT AT ALL: size it so TOTAL PROMPT VOLUME across all permutations -- not unique keys -- stays inside the budget. At 29,696 B/token that is budget_bytes / 29,696 / ldp_num_permutations tokens per request; with the 4.5 GB default and P=2 that is ~75,000 tokens per request, well short of the 131,072 window. Filling the context window and exercising the offload path are, on this box, mutually exclusive. ALSO CHECK: ollama was found running on the node during this crash (dmesg shows Comm: ollama). run_sweep.sh's prereqs require it stopped -- `sudo systemctl disable --now ollama` -- and it was not. It is a contributing factor of unknown size, not the cause. MODEL MUST BE THE HF REPO ID: this workload sizes contexts in exact tokens, so it calls AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model) on the SAME string it puts in the request payload. ldqa_max_output_length must stay exactly 128 -- upstream sentinel, see the NVFP4 copy.
